facts.text: Pomeroy was officially incorporated on February 3, 1886, after being platted in 1878 and becoming Garfield County seat in 1882.
The town’s name honors President James A. Garfield, whose name the county was also given when the legislature formed it in 1881.
The Eastern Washington Agricultural Museum, an 8,600‑sq‑ft hall, showcases farm machinery from the late 1800s to the 1950s, reflecting the region’s agrarian roots.
A historic brick building on Arlington Street houses the Denny Ashby Library, the county’s primary repository of local history and genealogy records.
Lewis and Clark passed through the area in 1805, long before Pomeroy was founded, marking the first recorded Caucasian visit to the region.
Captain Benjamin Bonneville surveyed the future town site in 1834, making Pomeroy one of the earliest surveyed locations in Washington.
